Goal:
Create a Python implementation that is a 1:1 functional port of the reference application for this benchmark. For the same input, the official reference CLI and your rebuilt version must produce exactly the same observable result: exit status, stdout, and stderr.

Reference:
- Project: eza
- Source language: Rust
- Target language: Python
- Repository: https://github.com/eza-community/eza.git
- Release/tag: v0.23.3

- Local source copy: ./rust-reference
- Official reference CLI: read ./REFERENCE_BINARY.txt
- Behavior area: directory listing, long view, tree, sort, hidden, icons/colors disabled

Hard constraints:
- Do not use Docker.
- Do not search the internet.
- Do not look for, copy, adapt, vendor, install, or import an existing Python implementation, clone, wrapper, compatibility layer, or package for this application.
- Use ./rust-reference and the official reference CLI as the only functional sources of truth.
- Implement in Python.
- Do not shell out to the official reference CLI from your implementation.
- Do not install packages that already implement this application or its command suite.
- The root deliverable must include ./compile.sh.
- ./compile.sh must build or wrap your Python implementation and leave a runnable root command named ./executable. On Windows, ./executable.exe or ./executable.cmd is also accepted.
- The first entrypoint discovered by the evaluator must itself be directly runnable on the current OS/runtime; do not leave a higher-priority wrapper, placeholder, or script that requires a different interpreter than the evaluator will use.
- The harness will run ./compile.sh and then invoke your runnable executable with the same argv used for the official reference CLI.

Deliverable shape:
- Keep the actual implementation in one or more Python files, for example ./main.py or ./eza_port.py.
- ./compile.sh must be idempotent and must create only entrypoints that are directly runnable by the evaluator on this machine.
- The evaluator checks entrypoints in this order: ./executable, ./executable.exe, ./executable.cmd, ./executable.bat, ./executable.js, ./executable.py, ./executable.jar.
- For a Python target, if ./executable exists, it must be valid Python source that can be run as: python ./executable <args>. Do not make ./executable a POSIX shell script.
- On Windows, prefer creating ./executable.cmd that calls your Python file. If you create ./executable.cmd, remove any POSIX shell wrapper named ./executable so it cannot be discovered first.
- On Unix-like systems, either make ./executable valid Python source with a Python shebang or make sure the current evaluator will not run it through the wrong interpreter.
- Do not leave stale, broken, placeholder, or higher-priority entrypoints in the workspace after ./compile.sh runs.

Equivalence requirements:
- For every evaluated invocation, running the official reference CLI and running your rebuilt executable with the same argv, stdin, files, and environment must produce the same exit status, stdout, and stderr.
- If the official binary prints nothing, your program must print nothing.
- If the official binary writes to stderr, your program must write to stderr.

Do not ask the user questions. Infer from source and official CLI behavior.

+    def lstat(self):

+    def is_file(self) -> bool:

+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:

+    except ValueError as exc:
+        print(f"eza: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 3
+
+    try:
+        lines = render(opts)
+    except BrokenPipeError:
+        return 0
+    if lines:
+        sys.stdout.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
+    return 0
+
+
+def parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> Options:

+    parser.add_argument("paths", nargs="*")
+    parser.add_argument("-l", "--long", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("-T", "--tree", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("-R", "--recurse", action="store_true")

+    parser.add_argument("--absolute", nargs="?", const="on", default="off")
+    parser.add_argument("--color", "--colour", nargs="?", const="auto")
+    parser.add_argument("--icons", nargs="?", const="auto")
+    parser.add_argument("--no-user", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--no-time", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--no-filesize", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--no-permissions", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--header", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--git", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--git-ignore", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--binary", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--bytes", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--no-quotes", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--version", "-v", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--help", "-?", action="store_true")
+    ns, unknown = parser.parse_known_args(argv)
+
+    if ns.help:
+        print("Usage: eza [options] [files...]", file=sys.stdout)
+        raise SystemExit(0)
+    if ns.version:
+        print("eza - A modern, maintained replacement for ls", file=sys.stdout)
+        raise SystemExit(0)
+    if unknown:
+        raise ValueError(f"unrecognised option '{unknown[0]}'")
+    sort_key = SORT_ALIASES.get(str(ns.sort).lower())
+    if sort_key is None:
+        raise ValueError(f"invalid sort field '{ns.sort}'")
+    return Options(
+        paths=ns.paths or ["."],
+        long=ns.long,
+        tree=ns.tree,
+        recurse=ns.recurse,
+        all=ns.all,
+        almost_all=ns.almost_all,
+        reverse=ns.reverse,
+        sort=sort_key,
+        dirs_first=ns.group_directories_first,
+        dirs_last=ns.group_directories_last,
+        only_dirs=ns.only_dirs,
+        only_files=ns.only_files,
+        no_symlinks=ns.no_symlinks,
+        classify=ns.classify not in (None, "never"),
+        absolute=ns.absolute,
+        level=ns.level,
+        no_user=ns.no_user,
+        no_time=ns.no_time,
+        no_filesize=ns.no_filesize,
+        no_permissions=ns.no_permissions,
+        header=ns.header,
+        oneline=ns.oneline,
+        grid=ns.grid,
+        width=ns.width,
+        ignore_globs=ns.ignore_glob,
+    )
+
+
+def render(opts: Options) -> list[str]:
+    paths = [Path(p) for p in opts.paths]
+    if opts.tree:
+        return render_tree_roots(paths, opts)
+    if opts.recurse:
+        return render_recurse(paths, opts)
+    return render_flat(paths, opts)
+
+
+def render_flat(paths: list[Path], opts: Options) -> list[str]:
+    targets: list[Entry] = []
+    errors: list[str] = []
+    multi = len(paths) > 1
+    out: list[str] = []
+    dirs: list[Path] = []
+    for path in paths:
+        if not path.exists() and not path.is_symlink():
+            errors.append(f"eza: {path}: No such file or directory")
+        elif path.is_dir() and not opts.only_files:
+            dirs.append(path)
+        else:
+            targets.append(Entry(path))
+    for msg in errors:
+        print(msg, file=sys.stderr)
+    if targets:
+        out.extend(format_entries(sort_entries(targets, opts), opts))
+    for idx, directory in enumerate(dirs):
+        if out or multi:
+            if out:
+                out.append("")
+            if multi:
+                out.append(f"{display_path(directory, opts)}:")
+        entries = list_dir(directory, opts)
+        out.extend(format_entries(entries, opts))
+    return out
+
+
+def render_recurse(paths: list[Path], opts: Options) -> list[str]:
+    out: list[str] = []
+    roots = [p for p in paths if p.exists() or p.is_symlink()]
+    for root_index, root in enumerate(roots):
+        if root_index:
+            out.append("")
+        if root.is_dir():
+            if len(roots) > 1 or root_index > 0:
+                out.append(f"{display_path(root, opts)}:")
+            entries = list_dir(root, opts)
+            out.extend(format_entries(entries, opts))
+            add_recurse_dirs(out, root, opts, 1)
+        else:
+            out.extend(format_entries([Entry(root)], opts))
+    return out
+
+
+def add_recurse_dirs(out: list[str], root: Path, opts: Options, depth: int) -> None:
+    if opts.level is not None and depth >= opts.level:
+        return
+    for entry in list_dir(root, opts):
+        if entry.is_dir() and not entry.is_symlink():
+            out.append("")
+            out.append(f"{display_path(entry.path, opts)}:")
+            children = list_dir(entry.path, opts)
+            out.extend(format_entries(children, opts))
+            add_recurse_dirs(out, entry.path, opts, depth + 1)
+
+
+def render_tree_roots(paths: list[Path], opts: Options) -> list[str]:
+    out: list[str] = []
+    for index, root in enumerate(paths):
+        if index:
+            out.append("")
+        out.append(display_path(root, opts))
+        if root.is_dir():
+            children = list_dir(root, opts)
+            add_tree_children(out, children, opts, "", 1)
+    return out
+
+
+def add_tree_children(out: list[str], entries: list[Entry], opts: Options, prefix: str, depth: int) -> None:
+    if opts.level is not None and depth > opts.level:
+        return
+    for index, entry in enumerate(entries):
+        last = index == len(entries) - 1
+        branch = "└── " if last else "├── "
+        out.append(prefix + branch + format_entry(entry, opts, tree_name_only=True))
+        if entry.is_dir() and not entry.is_symlink():
+            extension = "    " if last else "│   "
+            add_tree_children(out, list_dir(entry.path, opts), opts, prefix + extension, depth + 1)
+
+
+def list_dir(path: Path, opts: Options) -> list[Entry]:
+    try:
+        entries = [Entry(path / name, path) for name in os.listdir(path)]
+    except OSError as exc:
+        print(f"eza: {path}: {exc.strerror}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return []
+    entries = [e for e in entries if visible(e.name, opts)]
+    if opts.ignore_globs:
+        entries = [e for e in entries if not any(fnmatch.fnmatch(e.name, pat) for pat in opts.ignore_globs or [])]
+    if opts.only_dirs:
+        entries = [e for e in entries if e.is_dir()]
+    if opts.only_files:
+        entries = [e for e in entries if e.is_file() and not e.is_dir()]
+    if opts.no_symlinks:
+        entries = [e for e in entries if not e.is_symlink()]
+    return sort_entries(entries, opts)
+
+
+def visible(name: str, opts: Options) -> bool:
+    if opts.all:
+        return True
+    if opts.almost_all:
+        return name not in (".", "..")
+    return not name.startswith(".")
+
+
+def sort_entries(entries: list[Entry], opts: Options) -> list[Entry]:
+    if opts.sort == "none":
+        sorted_entries = list(entries)
+    else:
+        sorted_entries = sorted(entries, key=lambda e: sort_tuple(e, opts.sort))
+    if opts.reverse:
+        sorted_entries.reverse()
+    if opts.dirs_first:
+        sorted_entries.sort(key=lambda e: not e.is_dir())
+    elif opts.dirs_last:
+        sorted_entries.sort(key=lambda e: e.is_dir())
+    return sorted_entries
+
+
+def sort_tuple(entry: Entry, field: str):
+    name = entry.name.casefold()
+    try:
+        st = entry.lstat()
+    except OSError:
+        st = None
+    if field == "size":
+        return (0 if st is None else st.st_size, name)
+    if field == "modified" or field == "newest":
+        return (0 if st is None else -st.st_mtime, name)
+    if field == "oldest":
+        return (0 if st is None else st.st_mtime, name)
+    if field == "changed":
+        return (0 if st is None else -st.st_ctime, name)
+    if field == "accessed":
+        return (0 if st is None else -st.st_atime, name)
+    if field == "created":
+        return (0 if st is None else -getattr(st, "st_birthtime", st.st_ctime), name)
+    if field == "type":
+        return (type_rank(entry), name)
+    if field == "ext":
+        return (entry.path.suffix.casefold().lstrip("."), name)
+    return (name,)
+
+
+def type_rank(entry: Entry) -> int:
+    if entry.is_dir():
+        return 0
+    if entry.is_symlink():
+        return 1
+    return 2
+
+
+def format_entries(entries: list[Entry], opts: Options) -> list[str]:
+    if opts.long:
+        rows = [format_entry(e, opts) for e in entries]
+        if opts.header:
+            labels = []
+            if not opts.no_permissions:
+                labels.append("Permissions")
+            if not opts.no_filesize:
+                labels.append("Size")
+            if not opts.no_user:
+                labels.append("User")
+            if not opts.no_time:
+                labels.append("Date Modified")
+            labels.append("Name")
+            return [" ".join(labels)] + rows
+        return rows
+    names = [format_entry(e, opts) for e in entries]
+    if opts.oneline or opts.grid or len(names) <= 1:
+        return names
+    return names
+
+
+def format_entry(entry: Entry, opts: Options, tree_name_only: bool = False) -> str:
+    name = display_name(entry, opts)
+    if tree_name_only and not opts.long:
+        return name
+    if not opts.long:
+        return name
+    parts: list[str] = []
+    try:
+        st = entry.lstat()
+    except OSError:
+        st = None
+    if not opts.no_permissions:
+        parts.append(mode_string(st.st_mode if st else 0))
+    if not opts.no_filesize:
+        parts.append(format_size(st.st_size if st else 0))
+    if not opts.no_user:
+        parts.append(owner_name(st.st_uid if st and hasattr(st, "st_uid") else None))
+    if not opts.no_time:
+        parts.append(format_time(st.st_mtime if st else 0))
+    parts.append(name)
+    return " ".join(parts)
+
+
+def display_name(entry: Entry, opts: Options) -> str:
+    base = display_path(entry.path, opts) if entry.display_parent is None else entry.name
+    if entry.is_symlink():
+        try:
+            base += f" -> {os.readlink(entry.path)}"
+        except OSError:
+            pass
+    if opts.classify:
+        if entry.is_dir() and not entry.is_symlink():
+            base += "/"
+        elif is_executable(entry):
+            base += "*"
+    return base
+
+
+def display_path(path: Path, opts: Options) -> str:
+    if opts.absolute in ("on", "follow"):
+        try:
+            return str(path.resolve() if opts.absolute == "follow" else path.absolute())
+        except OSError:
+            return str(path.absolute())
+    return str(path).replace("\\", "/")
+
+
+def is_executable(entry: Entry) -> bool:
+    try:
+        return bool(entry.lstat().st_mode & stat.S_IXUSR) and not entry.is_dir()
+    except OSError:
+        return False
+
+
+def mode_string(mode: int) -> str:
+    prefix = "d" if stat.S_ISDIR(mode) else "l" if stat.S_ISLNK(mode) else "-"
+    bits = ""
+    for who in (stat.S_IRUSR, stat.S_IWUSR, stat.S_IXUSR, stat.S_IRGRP, stat.S_IWGRP, stat.S_IXGRP, stat.S_IROTH, stat.S_IWOTH, stat.S_IXOTH):
+        if not mode & who:
+            bits += "-"
+        elif who in (stat.S_IRUSR, stat.S_IRGRP, stat.S_IROTH):
+            bits += "r"
+        elif who in (stat.S_IWUSR, stat.S_IWGRP, stat.S_IWOTH):
+            bits += "w"
+        else:
+            bits += "x"
+    return prefix + bits
+
+
+def format_size(size: int) -> str:
+    if size < 1000:
+        return str(size)
+    units = ["k", "M", "G", "T"]
+    value = float(size)
+    unit = ""
+    for unit in units:
+        value /= 1000.0
+        if value < 1000.0:
+            break
+    return f"{value:.1f}{unit}"
+
+
+def owner_name(uid) -> str:
+    if uid is None:
+        return "-"
+    if os.name == "nt":
+        return "-"
+    try:
+        import pwd
+
+        return pwd.getpwuid(uid).pw_name
+    except Exception:
+        return str(uid)
+
+
+def format_time(timestamp: float) -> str:
+    tm = time.localtime(timestamp)
+    return time.strftime("%d %b %Y", tm).lstrip("0")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())
*** End Patch
